lines.text: Ants, or us: who weighs more? Every ant on Earth, on one scale.
lines.phonemes: ˈænts, ɔːɹ ˌʌs: hˌuː wˈeɪz mˈɔːɹ? ˈɛvɹi ˈænt ˌɔn ˈɜːθ, ˌɔn wˈʌn skˈeɪl.

lines.text: Decades ago, two of the world's great ant scientists sat down with this exact sum, and decided the scale would roughly balance.
lines.phonemes: dˈɛkeɪdz ɐɡˈoʊ, tˈuː ʌvðə wˈɜːldz ɡɹˈeɪt ˈænt sˈaɪəntɪsts sˈæt dˌaʊn wɪð ðɪs ɛɡzˈækt sˈʌm, ænd dᵻsˈaɪdᵻd ðə skˈeɪl wʊd ɹˈʌfli bˈæləns.

lines.text: Then a team gathered hundreds of real ant counts, from forests, deserts and cities, and found about twice as many ants as anyone had guessed.
lines.phonemes: ðˈɛn ɐ tˈiːm ɡˈæðɚd hˈʌndɹɪdz ʌv ɹˈiːəl ˈænt kˈaʊnts, fɹʌm fˈɔːɹɪsts, dˈɛzɚts ænd sˈɪɾiz, ænd fˈaʊnd ɐbˌaʊt twˈaɪs æz mˈɛni ˈænts æz ˈɛnɪwˌʌn hæd ɡˈɛst.

lines.text: So the ants should win. But a real ant is tinier than the old guess assumed, and once they're weighed properly, all of them together come to only about a fifth of us.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðɪ ˈænts ʃˌʊd wˈɪn. bˌʌt ɐ ɹˈiːəl ˈænt ɪz tˈaɪniɚ ðɐn ðɪ ˈoʊld ɡˈɛs ɐsˈuːmd, ænd wˈʌns ðeɪɚ wˈeɪd pɹˈɑːpɚli, ˈɔːl ʌv ðˌɛm təɡˌɛðɚ kˈʌm tʊ ˈoʊnli ɐbˌaʊt ɐ fˈɪfθ ʌv ˌʌs.

lines.text: That's still more than every wild bird and mammal on Earth combined. And for each one of us, there are about two and a half million ants.
lines.phonemes: ðæts stˈɪl mˈɔːɹ ðɐn ˈɛvɹi wˈaɪld bˈɜːd ænd mˈæməl ˌɔn ˈɜːθ kəmbˈaɪnd. ænd fɔːɹ ˈiːtʃ wˈʌn ʌv ˌʌs, ðɛɹˌɑːɹ ɐbˌaʊt tˈuː ænd ɐ hˈæf mˈɪliən ˈænts.

lines.text: Take the heaviest estimate anyone has published, and we still win the scale.
lines.phonemes: tˈeɪk ðə hˈɛviɪst ˈɛstᵻmət ˈɛnɪwˌʌn hɐz pˈʌblɪʃt, ænd wiː stˈɪl wˈɪn ðə skˈeɪl.

lines.text: So we win on the scale, by a lot. But they win on the count.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ wiː wˈɪn ɔnðə skˈeɪl, baɪ ɐ lˈɑːt. bˌʌt ðeɪ wˈɪn ɔnðə kˈaʊnt.

lines.text: Next envelope: how long would it take to count to a billion?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ wʊd ɪt tˈeɪk tə kˈaʊnt tʊ ɐ bˈɪliən?
